evals.prompt: Create a Word document called quarterly-summary.docx with the title "Q3 Summary", a 3-row table (a header row plus two data rows of metric/value), and a bulleted list of three takeaways.
evals.expected_output: A new, valid .docx authored with docx-js containing the title, a 3-row table, and a 3-item bulleted list.
expectations: A new .docx file is produced
The file is a valid OOXML package: it opens as a zip containing word/document.xml and validate.py reports it valid
The create path was used (docx-js via node / create_docx.cjs), not a hand-assembled zip
The document contains a title, a table with exactly 3 rows, and a bulleted list with 3 items
No python-docx, pandoc, LibreOffice/soffice, or other system tools were used

evals.prompt: In contract.docx, change the contract term from "twelve months" to "twenty-four months" as a tracked change so a reviewer can accept or reject it.
evals.expected_output: contract.docx (or a copy) where 'twelve months' is deleted and 'twenty-four months' inserted as a Word tracked change, and the package still validates.
expectations: The edit is a tracked change: 'twelve months' is wrapped in w:del/w:delText and 'twenty-four months' in w:ins/w:t with a unique w:id
No w:t element appears inside a w:del
validate.py reports the resulting package as valid
Reading the result with mammoth (accepted view) shows 'twenty-four months' and not 'twelve months'
The unpack/edit/validate/pack round-trip was used (e.g. edit_text.py --tracked), not string replacement on the raw .docx
No python-docx, pandoc, LibreOffice/soffice, or other system tools were used

evals.prompt: Summarize what contract.docx says in a few bullet points.
evals.expected_output: A short text or Markdown summary reflecting the document's actual content (payment terms, term length, responsibilities).
expectations: Document text was extracted with mammoth (read_docx.py)
The summary reflects real content of the document, e.g. the 30-day payment term and the twelve-month term
No python-docx, pandoc, LibreOffice/soffice, or other system tools were used

evals.prompt: Add a comment on the first paragraph of contract.docx that says "Please confirm these terms with legal."
evals.expected_output: contract.docx (or a copy) with a Word comment anchored in the first paragraph, still a valid package.
expectations: A word/comments.xml part exists containing the comment text
[Content_Types].xml has an Override for /word/comments.xml and word/_rels/document.xml.rels has a comments relationship
document.xml contains w:commentRangeStart and w:commentRangeEnd plus a w:commentReference sharing one w:id
validate.py reports the resulting package as valid
The comment.py flow was used
No python-docx, pandoc, LibreOffice/soffice, or other system tools were used
